title: Conditional evidence integration and the incremental contribution of sheaf structure in controlled-synthetic groundwater benchmarks
scope: The study uses a MODFLOW/MODPATH flow-tracer-chemistry generator for the process-based integration and public-pipeline audits, a separate scalar affine generator for the representation benchmark and estimator diagnostic, and a descriptive Northern Ghana scope audit. Results are conditional capability tests, not whole-framework or field validation.

objectives.statement: Quantify the incremental topology-ranking contribution of hydraulic, age and chemical evidence, alone, in pairs and combined, under native and adverse (permuted) conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Native panel PR-AUC/ROC-AUC/Brier/log-loss/entropy/ECE reported for all seven evidence panels
Case-block bootstrap contrasts reported for native and permuted conditions with 95% CIs
Predeclared conflict diagnostic reported including its sensitivity outcome

objectives.statement: Quantify how correct, partial and reversed topology assumptions change groundwater-age accuracy, interval width and coverage under an informative and a weak tracer regime.
acceptance_criteria: Age MAE, bias, 95% coverage and interval width reported for four topology conditions and two tracer regimes
Importance-sampling ESS and log mean weight reported per case/regime
Paired case-block bootstrap contrasts reported for correct/partial/reversed vs no-topology

objectives.statement: Quantify reaction-family recovery under core and enhanced hydrochemical indicator panels, with carbonate processes reported separately.
acceptance_criteria: Modal-family accuracy, true-family probability, support entropy and effective supported families reported per process and panel
Carbonate weathering and precipitation reported separately from aggregate accuracy

objectives.statement: Audit the Northern Ghana workbook to separate supportable component diagnostics from non-identifiable field claims.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence-availability audit reported (chemistry, isotopes, age tracers, screen intervals, coordinates, connectivity)
Explicit claim boundary reported distinguishing supportable from non-identifiable interpretations

objectives.statement: Quantify what affine restriction maps and a global section contribute beyond edge-local and identity-Laplacian weighted graphs.
acceptance_criteria: Competence-matched edge-local graph, identity-Laplacian, affine-sheaf and permuted-map conditions evaluated on a locked test split
Paired case-block PR-AUC, Brier and conflict-localisation contrasts reported with predeclared claim rules
Fresh-seed robust/global/hybrid estimators and separately cross-fitted calibration evaluated under a second two-stage lock

inputs.provenance: run_m7_3_nonuniqueness.py locked run, protocol commit d336e87
Two-stage prospectively locked one-time M7.5 confirmatory run

risks.risk: Synthetic truth is model-conditioned and could be mistaken for field validation
risks.mitigation: Explicit claim guardrails in Outline.md, Methods, Discussion and Conclusion distinguishing synthetic from field truth

risks.risk: Reduced posterior uncertainty could be misread as improved inference under evidence misspecification
risks.mitigation: Predeclared adverse (permutation) controls and paired discrimination/calibration metrics reported alongside entropy

risks.risk: A sheaf-versus-graph comparison could attribute gains to unequal calibration, tuning or optimisers
risks.mitigation: Shared and separately cross-fitted calibration regimes, identical numerical solver in the identity limit, equal-dimensional features, frozen development selection, and permuted-map controls
